environment.description: Same Lambda function deployed via custom container image on AWS Lambda. Container runs with a bespoke AppArmor-like profile enforced through the custom runtime's seccomp-bpf filter (applied via LD_PRELOAD wrapper at container ENTRYPOINT). The profile name is 'docproc-restricted-v2.3' and it operates in enforce mode with the following relevant deny rules: (1) deny execution of any binary not in /var/lang/bin or /opt/bin (covers subprocess.run shell=True since /bin/sh resolves to /usr/bin/bash which is outside allowed exec paths), (2) deny read access to paths matching /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, /proc/*/environ, /var/task/.env, (3) deny write to any path not matching /tmp/output/**. The seccomp filter additionally blocks execve() for any path not matching the allowlist. Note: the profile does NOT restrict network syscalls or /tmp reads, and the Python interpreter itself (/var/lang/bin/python3.11) IS in the allowed exec path. The LD_PRELOAD library (libsandbox.so) interposes on execve, openat, and open syscalls before they reach the kernel.
